If your query is from 2026 but you fetch only 2025–2026 epi data, the "how did it behave historically" sections have nothing to compare against. A decade or more is a good default.
  6. --skip_literature true --skip_iqtree true — optional speed-ups used in this example.
  7. -resume — cached tasks are reused; only steps whose inputs changed re-run.

docs.title: What the run produces for the dashboard
docs.text: Output Feeds results/pathogen_identification/<species>/ Biological Threat tables & charts results/knowledge_warehouse/knowledge_warehouse.duckdb Trees, tips, samples, epi records — most analytical panels results/transmission_context/<species>/*.tsv Transmission & Spread, geographic panels results/pathogen_mutation_profile/<species>/ Mutation landscape, PLS-DA results/intelligence_brief/<species>/intelligence_brief.json Overview narrative + Intelligence Brief results/*/auspice/*.json Phylogenetic trees, tip metadata (clades, dates, geography) results/epi_raw/ + epi tables FluNet / HDX / EMPRES-i historical context

docs.title: Typical durations
docs.text: A mixed Ebola + influenza run of a few genomes takes roughly 45 minutes to 2 hours on a laptop, dominated by Nextstrain builds and sequence annotation. With -resume, re-runs only redo what changed (usually BUILD_KNOWLEDGE_DB → COMPUTE_TRANSMISSION_CONTEXT onward).

docs.title: Interpreting epidemiological context
docs.text:
Section in progress

This page will explain where the epidemiological layer comes from (WHO FluNet for influenza, HDX / EMPRES-i for Ebola and avian influenza), how --epi_min_year / --epi_max_year shape the historical comparison, and how R(t) at sampling is estimated.

docs.title: Key idea
docs.text: The transmission and geographic panels are only as good as the epi window fetched at run time. Historical questions need a window wide enough to contain history — see Running the pipeline.

docs.title: Interpreting genomic results
docs.text:
Section in progress

A compact reference for the metrics used across the dashboard: clade / lineage labels, genetic distance, divergence (substs/site), % identity, genome coverage, PLS-DA VIP scores, mutation burden, and what counts as a "novelty signal".

docs.title: Quick glossary (will be expanded)
docs.text: Term Meaning in the dashboard Clade / lineage Named phylogenetic group assigned by Nextclade or the build's own labels (clade_membership for seasonal flu, label_clade for avian flu, clade for Ebola) Genetic distance Distance to the closest reference genome — fraction or raw count depending on data availability; elevated values are a novelty signal Divergence Root-to-tip distance in substitutions/site on the tree MSA identity Mean pairwise identity of the query within the multiple-sequence alignment VIP score Variable-importance-in-projection from PLS-DA — how much each protein separates query from background

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: The dashboard is built to show what the data supports — and to say so when the support is thin. Keep these caveats in mind when quoting results.

docs.title: Evidence labels
docs.text: Panels are labelled observed history, estimated (model fitted to observed data, e.g. R(t), growth-rate fits), or tree-derived. Nothing on the dashboard forecasts future cases — that capability was removed because the pipeline does not collect enough covariates to project responsibly.

docs.title: Structural limitations
docs.text:
• Background sampling bias — the tree's "history" is whatever genomes the builds downloaded. Unsampled transmission is invisible to every panel.
  • Assessment heuristic is triage, not risk assessment — MONITOR / INVESTIGATE / ESCALATE uses only identification signals today (see Intelligence Overview).
  • Country-level coordinates — background genomes map at country centroids unless finer locations exist; "origin" means earliest sampled, not true geographic origin.
  • Segmented-genome nuance (influenza) — the same isolate can carry different clade labels per segment (reassortment); HA labels take priority in the warehouse.
  • LLM narratives — Ollama-written text is grounded on the computed facts but can phrase them loosely; the numbers to trust are in the tables.
  • Epi coverage varies — FluNet/HDX/EMPRES-i reporting is uneven across countries and years; absence of a signal is not evidence of absence.

docs.title: Informing public-health decisions
docs.text:

This page will map each dashboard section to the decision it supports: triage (Intelligence Overview), confirmatory sequencing priorities (Biological Threat), importation vs local transmission (Geographic), cluster response (Transmission & Spread), and preparedness framing (Countermeasure Readiness, Evidence & Knowledge Gaps).
